title: World Heritage Atlas Quiz Bank
description: Questions are stored separately from site records and resolved by scope. General questions apply to all sites; specialized questions target exact site IDs; site_type questions apply to programme keys.

scopes.label: Specialized · this site
scopes.description: Targets one or more exact site IDs.

scopes.label: Site type
scopes.description: Targets UNESCO programme keys such as World Heritage, Global Geopark or Biosphere Reserve.

quizzes.question: Which action usually prevents the most waste before recycling is needed?
options: Buy less and reuse or repair items
Buy more single-use items made from recyclable material
Mix all waste together
Burn waste in the open
quizzes.explanation: Waste prevention and reuse avoid material use in the first place; recycling is useful but still requires collection and processing.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNEP — Beat Plastic Pollution

quizzes.question: How can a plastic wrapper dropped on a street reach the ocean?
options: Rain and drains can carry it into streams and rivers
It dissolves immediately in soil
It always stays exactly where it was dropped
It turns into harmless sand overnight
quizzes.explanation: Litter can move through drains, waterways and rivers. Keeping waste out of the environment is more effective than trying to collect it later.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNEP — Beat Plastic Pollution

quizzes.question: What is the safest general rule when observing wild animals?
options: Keep a respectful distance and never feed them
Offer food to make photos easier
Touch young animals if they seem calm
Chase them until they move into view
quizzes.explanation: Feeding or approaching wildlife can change behaviour and create danger for people and animals. Follow local rules and trained guides.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — World Heritage and sustainable tourism

quizzes.question: What is a practical way to reduce pressure on a destination's water supply?
options: Avoid unnecessary water use and report leaks
Leave taps running while exploring
Assume water is unlimited wherever tourists visit
Dump oils or chemicals into drains
quizzes.explanation: Water-saving behaviour helps destinations where residents, ecosystems and visitors share limited supplies.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Education for Sustainable Development

quizzes.question: A social post claims a heritage building is 5,000 years old but gives no source. What should you do?
options: Check an authoritative record and look for evidence
Repeat it because the post has many likes
Treat every comment as a verified source
Change the date to make the story more exciting
quizzes.explanation: Popularity is not evidence. Compare claims with authoritative records, named sources and credible research; note when information remains uncertain.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre

quizzes.question: What is the best way to interpret an unfamiliar heritage place?
options: Consider its history, local context and multiple sources
Judge it only by modern appearance
Assume every monument had the same purpose
Ignore the people connected with the place
quizzes.explanation: Context helps explain why a place matters, how it changed, and how communities understand it today.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre

quizzes.question: Before recording or sharing a community's ceremony, song or story, what should you do?
options: Follow community protocols and ask for permission where appropriate
Assume public visibility means unrestricted permission
Record people secretly to keep the footage authentic
Remove all community context from the caption
quizzes.explanation: Living heritage belongs to the communities that practise and transmit it. Respect consent, cultural protocols, privacy and community decisions.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — What is Intangible Cultural Heritage?

quizzes.question: Why should visitors clean mud from footwear and gear when local guidance asks them to?
options: Mud and gear can carry seeds, organisms or pathogens between places
Clean footwear makes every ecosystem identical
It guarantees that no species can ever spread
It is only about keeping shoes attractive
quizzes.explanation: Organisms can be moved unintentionally between ecosystems. Follow destination-specific biosecurity guidance, especially on islands and protected areas.
quizzes.sourceLabel: Convention on Biological Diversity — Invasive Alien Species

quizzes.question: Which visitor choice generally has the lowest impact on a sensitive site?
options: Use marked paths and follow local access rules
Climb fragile structures for a better view
Take rocks or artefacts as souvenirs
Leave food waste for animals
quizzes.explanation: Marked paths and access rules help protect fragile surfaces, habitats and visitor safety. Never remove heritage material or feed wildlife.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — World Heritage and sustainable tourism

quizzes.question: Why can protecting connected habitats be more effective than protecting isolated patches alone?
options: Many species need to move between feeding, breeding and shelter areas
Every species remains in one tiny location for life
Connections prevent all natural change
Only large animals use habitats
quizzes.explanation: Ecological connections can support movement, genetic exchange and resilience. The best approach depends on the species and landscape.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Biodiversity

quizzes.question: A coastal site faces more frequent flooding. Which is the strongest first step for planning?
options: Combine local knowledge, risk evidence and an adaptation plan
Wait for damage before collecting any information
Protect one building while ignoring residents and ecosystems
Assume historical weather will never change
quizzes.explanation: Risk-aware planning combines evidence, community experience and suitable adaptation options. Measures should fit local hazards and avoid shifting risk elsewhere.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Climate change and World Heritage

quizzes.question: If a traditional practice changes as younger people adapt it to present-day life, does that automatically make it inauthentic?
options: No; living heritage can evolve while communities continue to recognise it
Yes; every detail must remain frozen forever
Yes; only museum displays count as heritage
No; communities should have no say in how it changes
quizzes.explanation: Intangible heritage is living and transmitted between generations. Communities themselves play a central role in deciding how it is continued or adapted.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — What is Intangible Cultural Heritage?

quizzes.question: Which three symbolic realms are commonly used to explain Borobudur's vertical monument layout?
options: Kamadhatu, Rupadhatu and Arupadhatu
Earth, ocean and atmosphere
Past, present and future
Java, Sumatra and Bali
quizzes.explanation: These terms describe realms associated broadly with desire, form and formlessness in Buddhist cosmology. Interpretations should be read alongside reliable heritage resources and local expertise.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Borobudur

quizzes.question: When studying Borobudur's relief panels, what helps a visitor interpret them responsibly?
options: Use the sequence, iconography and authoritative interpretation instead of guessing from one panel
Assume every panel is a modern decoration
Touch or rub the carvings to understand their texture
Treat every panel as a record of a single literal event
quizzes.explanation: Reliefs are part of a larger architectural and narrative programme. Context, preservation guidance and expert interpretation are more reliable than a guess from an isolated image.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Borobudur

quizzes.question: The principal temple at Prambanan is dedicated to which Hindu deity?
options: Shiva
Poseidon
Thor
Quetzalcoatl
quizzes.explanation: Prambanan is a major Hindu temple compound; its central and largest temple is dedicated to Shiva.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Prambanan

quizzes.question: What is a responsible way to help conserve Prambanan's stone architecture during a visit?
options: Follow barriers and do not climb, scratch or touch fragile surfaces where prohibited
Climb temple structures for a better photograph
Write initials on an inconspicuous stone
Remove small fragments as souvenirs
quizzes.explanation: Visitor behaviour can contribute to physical wear or damage. Follow site rules and protect carved stone and structural elements.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Prambanan

quizzes.question: Why should conservation planning at Komodo consider both land and sea?
options: Terrestrial and marine habitats are connected and support linked ecological processes
The sea has no influence on island ecosystems
Only one species matters in every habitat
Marine habitats are outside nature conservation
quizzes.explanation: Komodo's importance includes terrestrial wildlife and marine biodiversity. Conservation decisions should consider ecological connections and site-specific evidence.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Komodo National Park

quizzes.question: What is the safest response if a Komodo dragon is nearby on a trail?
options: Follow ranger instructions, keep distance and do not feed or approach it
Try to feed it for a close-up photograph
Separate a young animal from its group
Run toward it to make it move
quizzes.explanation: Komodo dragons are wild predators. Follow park rules and trained ranger guidance; do not approach, feed or provoke wildlife.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Komodo National Park

quizzes.question: What is the subak system best understood as?
options: A community-based cooperative system for managing irrigation water in Bali
A single stone temple used only for tourism
A modern factory for rice production
A method for replacing all local farming traditions
quizzes.explanation: Subak connects water management, farming communities and cultural-religious institutions. It is a social and landscape system, not just a canal network.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Cultural Landscape of Bali Province

quizzes.question: Why are water temples relevant to understanding Bali's subak landscape?
options: They are part of the cultural and institutional relationships associated with water management
They exist only as decorative monuments with no local context
They prove irrigation never requires cooperation
They are unrelated to the landscape's cultural significance
quizzes.explanation: The nominated landscape expresses relationships among water temples, agricultural practices and cooperative water management. Local practice and historical context matter.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Cultural Landscape of Bali Province

quizzes.question: Why do researchers study the geological layer in which a fossil was found?
options: Its context helps interpret the fossil's age, environment and relationship to other evidence
The layer is irrelevant once a fossil is cleaned
All fossils from one region must be the same age
A fossil alone always provides a complete history
quizzes.explanation: Stratigraphy and geological context help researchers build and test interpretations of human evolution and past environments.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Sangiran Early Man Site

quizzes.question: Which approach is most appropriate when a new fossil discovery is reported?
options: Document its location and context, then assess it using scientific methods
Move it immediately and discard location notes
Identify its species from a social-media photo alone
Assume it changes all existing scientific knowledge at once
quizzes.explanation: Documentation and context preserve scientific value. Conclusions should follow careful analysis and comparison with existing evidence.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Sangiran Early Man Site

quizzes.question: Why can a large protected area spanning different elevations support varied ecosystems?
options: Temperature, moisture and habitat conditions can change with elevation
Elevation has no effect on habitat
Every species requires exactly the same climate
Only the highest point can support life
quizzes.explanation: Elevation gradients can create different habitat conditions and ecological communities. The actual pattern varies across the landscape.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Lorentz National Park

quizzes.question: What is a sound reason to combine local knowledge with biodiversity research in a landscape like Lorentz?
options: Different evidence sources can complement each other when collected and interpreted respectfully
Local knowledge should automatically replace every scientific method
Scientific data means local communities should not be consulted
Only observations from tourists are useful
quizzes.explanation: Research and local knowledge can answer different questions. Collaboration should respect rights, protocols, evidence quality and community consent.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Lorentz National Park

quizzes.question: What is central to a place being inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List?
options: Its Outstanding Universal Value, assessed against the Convention's criteria
Its popularity on social media
The number of souvenirs sold nearby
Its age alone, regardless of significance
quizzes.explanation: World Heritage inscription depends on Outstanding Universal Value and the applicable criteria, alongside requirements for protection and management.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — About World Heritage

quizzes.question: What does the distinction between cultural, natural and mixed World Heritage properties describe?
options: The kinds of heritage values for which the property is recognised
The number of people allowed to visit every day
Whether a site must charge an entry fee
Whether a property has a visitor centre
quizzes.explanation: The categories reflect the basis of recognition under the World Heritage Convention; they are not visitor-service or popularity ratings.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — About World Heritage

quizzes.question: Does a Tentative List entry mean a property is already inscribed on the World Heritage List?
options: No; it is a property a State Party may consider for a future nomination
Yes; every Tentative List property is already inscribed
Yes, but only for natural properties
It means the property has been removed from heritage consideration
quizzes.explanation: A Tentative List is an inventory of properties a State Party may consider for nomination. A Tentative List entry is not the same as inscription.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Tentative Lists

quizzes.question: Who submits and updates a country's World Heritage Tentative List?
options: The State Party, through its national processes
Any visitor by adding a pin to an online map
A travel company acting without the country's involvement
A local business with no official process
quizzes.explanation: Tentative Lists are submitted by States Parties. A site's presence should not be presented as an inscription or guaranteed future nomination.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Tentative Lists

quizzes.question: What makes a UNESCO Global Geopark more than a collection of interesting rocks?
options: It connects internationally significant geological heritage with protection, education and sustainable development
It is only a list of mineral shops
It must exclude all communities from the area
It recognises only built monuments
quizzes.explanation: UNESCO Global Geoparks take a place-based approach that connects geological heritage with wider natural and cultural values, education and sustainable local development.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Global Geoparks

quizzes.question: How should a geopark's geological sites generally be managed?
options: Conserve their geological heritage while supporting education and responsible local development
Encourage visitors to remove representative rocks
Treat geology as unrelated to local culture and livelihoods
Promote unlimited access regardless of site sensitivity
quizzes.explanation: Geoconservation, education and sustainable development are complementary goals. Local rules and site-specific conservation needs still apply.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Global Geoparks

quizzes.question: What is the purpose of the core, buffer and transition areas in a biosphere reserve model?
options: They help combine conservation with compatible research, activities and sustainable development
They rank areas from most famous to least famous
They mean every activity is allowed in every zone
They separate people from nature in all circumstances
quizzes.explanation: Biosphere reserves use zonation to support conservation in core areas while allowing compatible activities, cooperation and sustainable development in surrounding zones.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Man and the Biosphere Programme

quizzes.question: Which approach best reflects the Man and the Biosphere Programme?
options: Connect biodiversity conservation with research, learning and sustainable livelihoods
Protect nature while ignoring how local people live
Focus only on visitor numbers
Replace every local management institution with tourism operators
quizzes.explanation: The programme promotes approaches that connect people and nature, conservation and sustainable development, with learning and cooperation across landscapes.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Man and the Biosphere Programme

quizzes.question: Which is an example of intangible cultural heritage?
options: A community's living performance, craft knowledge, oral tradition or festive practice
Only a stone building with no associated practice
Only an item stored in a museum
A tradition that the community no longer recognises but outsiders impose
quizzes.explanation: Intangible cultural heritage includes practices, expressions, knowledge and skills that communities recognise and transmit between generations.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — What is Intangible Cultural Heritage?

quizzes.question: Who should play a central role in safeguarding a living heritage practice?
options: The communities and practitioners who recognise and transmit it
Only outside researchers
Only a tourism company
Visitors who have no connection with the practice
quizzes.explanation: Safeguarding should respect the people who practise and transmit the heritage, including their rights, consent and choices about how it continues.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — What is Intangible Cultural Heritage?

quizzes.question: What is the broad aim of the UNESCO Creative Cities Network?
options: Use creativity and cultural industries as part of sustainable urban development
Rank cities only by the number of historic monuments
Replace local culture with a single global style
Certify that every business in a city is creative
quizzes.explanation: The network encourages cooperation among cities that place culture and creativity within sustainable development strategies.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Creative Cities Network

quizzes.question: Which action fits the idea of a creative city best?
options: Support local creators and connect culture with inclusive urban development
Measure success only by souvenir sales
Exclude community artists from city planning
Treat creativity as unrelated to jobs or public life
quizzes.explanation: Creative-city approaches connect cultural activity with social, economic and urban development, while respecting local diversity and community participation.
quizzes.sourceLabel: UNESCO — Creative Cities Network
